name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: the parts are worth more than the group trades for
frontmatter.summary: Update after Q3-2026. The nine-month actuals were already in the published update; the 28 October net-profit story re-reports the same release. We re-mark automotive and financial services on the run-rate, value the financing block on its own book/ROE-COE card, add holdco net cash and the effective UNTR stake. ADD at Rp5,006.
thesis: Cheap on its own history: the group trades on 5.6x FY2025 earnings and 0.8x of book, against own-history averages of 7.2x and 1.1x [S0].

Our look-through sum-of-the-parts marks the parts at Rp4,657 after holding the discount at 25%, above the Rp4,540 price; the price itself implies a 26.9% discount to the same marks, wider than the one we hold [S2, S14].

The clean nine-month result was flat on the prior year despite the Martabe outage and the coal-quota hit, with automotive and financial services growing and mining profit back to year-on-year growth in the third quarter [S14].
The bear case is a discount widening to the top of its persistent range with mining weak and credit costs higher; it is carried explicitly at Rp4,043 [S14, S5].

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: named and dated discount catalyst: the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is still ongoing with no disclosed end date [S8, S14, S16]; execution is disclosed at the FY2026 audited results, dated 30 April 2027 on the prior-year cadence [S4], alongside the May-2026 capital-allocation roadmap [S11]

blocks.text: **The news adds nothing.** The 28 October Kontan story on the year-on-year fall in nine-month net profit is a re-report of the same 28 October release that our published update already carried: every figure it cites is in the release and the LK, it adds no operating fact, and it changes neither the forecast nor the mark [S12, S14, S15].

**What changed in this revision.** The nine-month reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, but IDR2.96tn of the gap is a non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge; clean of it, profit was IDR24.57tn on revenue of IDR243.87tn [S14, S15]. Mining returned to year-on-year growth in the third quarter after a first half distorted by the Martabe outage and the coal quota [S14]. We move to **ADD** with a target of Rp5,006 against Rp4,540, an expected total return of 19.5% including Rp420 of dividends [S14, S15]. The rating change is the correction the red team's first point forces: once the unlisted blocks are marked on the nine-month actuals and the financing block on its own book/ROE-COE card, the sum-of-the-parts at the held discount is Rp4,657, only just above the price, and the undiscounted cross-checks are no longer allowed to close the gap through the blend [S15, S0].

The market is valuing the group as one declining business while its largest halves grow. In the first nine months automotive net income rose to IDR9.79tn and financial services to IDR7.15tn, while mining fell to IDR5.07tn [S14]; those three now earn about nine tenths of group profit [S2, S3]. The mining downturn is real but bounded, and the third quarter was its first improvement of the year [S14].

The marks now run on the actuals. The three listed stakes that are whole reported divisions — United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari and Astra Graphia — go in at market value on the audited or, for UNTR, the effective post-buyback stake [S6]; automotive and financial services, which the group reports separately, are marked on their nine-month attributable income annualised [S15], and financial services uses its own book/ROE-COE card rather than the parent's earnings multiple [S15]; the wider unlisted blocks stay on the group's own-history multiple because the nine-month disclosure no longer splits them [S0]. Holdco net cash adds to the mark instead of a double-counted debt deduction [S14]. We apply a 25% discount, inside the card's persistent range and narrower than the 26.9% the price implies [S2, S14]; the SOTP carries 96% of the weight, with the P/E and P/BV shown only as small cross-checks so they cannot close the discount arithmetic [S0]. The parts are worth Rp4,657 after the discount, above the Rp4,540 price.

Astra International is one of Indonesia's largest listed companies: more than three hundred subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates that sell, finance and service motor vehicles, distribute and contract heavy equipment, mine coal, gold and nickel, run toll roads, plantations, IT and property, and finance much of what they sell [S2]. From the first half of 2026 it reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as its three Core Businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3].

On the audited FY2025 divisional basis, net income attributable to the parent split as follows: Automotive & Mobility IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy IDR9.10tn, Agribusiness IDR1.17tn, Infrastructure IDR1.26tn, Information Technology IDR0.21tn and Property IDR0.72tn [S4]. Automotive is distribution and retail finance built on Toyota, Daihatsu, the Honda motorcycle joint venture and Otoparts [S4]; Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment is United Tractors with Pamapersada and Komatsu distribution, the largest earnings-volatility source [S4].

Strategy changed materially in 2026: a May roadmap focused the group on three core businesses, put every wider business under an earn-or-reallocate test, and tied leadership incentives to total shareholder return [S11]; in July shareholders approved a new buyback and a management share plan [S8]. Control sits with Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd at 50.1% of the shares, part of the Jardine Matheson group, with a 49.0% free float [S6, S0].

Astra began as a trading company in the late fifties and grew into a conglomerate by partnering with Japanese
industrial groups across vehicles, components and heavy machinery, then adding financial services. Much of its
profit still comes from joint ventures where it holds a minority economic interest but a controlling operating
role, and its minorities own a share of a structure that depends on those relationships continuing.

The Indonesian car market is the swing factor. National car sales fell through 2025, when Astra's share still reached 51.0% [S4]. They turned hard in 2026: national wholesales reached 679,000 units in the first nine months, up about a fifth, while Astra's own car sales grew more slowly and its share normalised to 49.0% [S14, S7]. The industry body expects the 850,000-unit full-year target to be met [S7]. The recovery is incomplete: the middle-income buyers who drove the last million-unit year have not returned, and purchasing power and access to financing remain the binding constraints [S9]. Motorcycles are the steadier franchise, with Honda holding 77.0% of the market [S14].

The heavy-equipment and mining complex is the mirror image, and the third quarter marked a turn. Over nine months Komatsu unit sales fell to 3,000 units and mining-contractor overburden removal to 766.0 million bank cubic metres as the national coal quota cut mining customers' capital spending [S14]. Coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped producing early in the year [S14]. But the division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted, which management expects to carry into the fourth quarter [S14]. This is a policy-driven cycle in a business Astra controls through UNTR.

The competitive position is durable but not invulnerable. Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading car brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles, while the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm a captive origination channel [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese entrants and electrified models, which the group meets through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. On heavy equipment the moat is Komatsu distribution plus the Pamapersada contractor, tied to the coal cycle [S2].

Regulation matters more here than for most conglomerates. The state sets the coal quota and has already cut heavy-equipment demand [S14]; vehicle taxes and subsidies shape the car market [S9]. The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and Bank Indonesia's policy rate at 5.8%, with inflation at 3.3%; a consumer-durable and consumer-financing group is rate-sensitive [S2, S4].

FY2025 profit before tax was IDR49,288.0bn against EBIT of IDR38,665.0bn, the gap being IDR9.62tn of permanent equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income; net income was IDR32,769.0bn and earnings per share Rp815 [S6].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, a gross margin just under twenty-two per cent [S15]. That is below the FY2025 rate because the first half held the Martabe outage and the coal-quota hit; the third quarter ran at a materially better margin as mining and gold recovered [S14]. Costs rose faster than revenue: selling expenses were IDR10.41tn and administrative expenses IDR16.94tn, over eleven per cent of revenue against about ten per cent in FY2025, so operating profit fell even though revenue held [S15].

The composition of the decline is the point. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, but IDR2.96tn of the fall came from non-recurring impairment and fair-value adjustments on equity investments, principally geothermal and nickel [S14]. Profit before tax was IDR30.01tn, below the operating line other income turned to an expense of IDR2.43tn from income a year earlier, and the share of joint-venture results rose to IDR8.13tn [S15]. Clean of the charge, net profit was IDR24.57tn, down about one per cent, and clean earnings per share was slightly higher on the smaller share count [S14].

The data pack carries no depreciation line for this direct-method filer, so we restate it from the audited notes: IDR17.87tn in FY2025 and IDR16.70tn in FY2024 [S6]. On that basis FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, an EBITDA margin of 17.5% [S6].

Cash generation is the strongest quality signal. Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn over nine months, above consolidated profit even as financing receivables grew [S15, S14]. Capital expenditure was IDR17,440.0bn in FY2025 and ran lower in the first nine months; dividends paid were IDR16,426.0bn, a payout of 50.0% the company describes as its policy ratio [S15, S0, S4].

The balance sheet reads better at the holding-company level. Group net debt was IDR56,315.0bn at FY2025 [S0], but almost all sits inside the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn at September 2026 [S14]. Excluding them the group was back to net cash of IDR1.80tn, having been in net debt at the June half-year after the Arafura acquisition and the buyback [S14, S2]; parent equity rose to IDR238.10tn [S15]. The dividend-upstream test passes: the parent received IDR18.99tn in FY2025 while paying IDR16.43tn to its own shareholders [S6].

Our forecast anchors on the actual nine months. Revenue grows 1.0% to IDR326,625.9bn, the flat nine months needing only the small fourth-quarter step-up guided [S14]. We cut the FY2026E gross margin to 21.7% and raised operating costs to 11.1% of revenue from the nine-month actual and a fourth quarter at the third quarter's rate, giving FY2026E operating profit of IDR34,524.4bn and an EBITDA margin of 16.1% [S15, S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate, but operating costs stay at the third-quarter 10.8% rather than reverting to the pre-2026 ratio, because no sourced cost programme justifies the lower figure [S15, S6]. We set other income at the clean nine-month run-rate annualised, IDR11,548bn, and carry the minority take at the actual clean nine-month share before a partial restoration as mining recovers [S15, S14]. Net income attributable to the parent is IDR33,362.8bn clean, broadly flat, then IDR36,107.6bn in FY2027E and IDR43,371.5bn by FY2030E; the forecast excludes the non-recurring charge, so reported FY2026 will be lower by roughly that amount.

Earnings-quality flags, run at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [S0], and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15], so the three-year accruals ratio is negative in every year. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and tied to equity investments, but we strip it before applying any multiple [S14]. **Margin and cost divergence** is the flag to follow: costs grew while revenue was flat, and we hold the higher ratio rather than banking operating leverage [S15]. **Financing-book provisioning** is the right test for the lender: the charge was built, not released, at IDR1.16tn in the first half while receivables grew to IDR132.00tn [S5, S14]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025 and sales IDR27.94tn [S6]; operating structures rather than siphon vehicles, both falling year on year. **Auditor** and **IDX notation** are flagged open checks: the archived LK omits the auditor's report pages and idx.co.id is not retrieved by policy, so we cannot confirm the opinion or the notation page; no going-concern, late-filing or special-monitoring notice appears in any archived disclosure [S6]. **Fixed-asset revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn in FY2025 [S6]. **Structure flags**: no pledged controlling stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum-of-the-parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book multiples at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.9% and WACC 11.9%, built from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.36 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.66) and a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% plus country risk of 2.5% [S0]. The discount axis matters far more than the rate axis in the sensitivity.

The primary method is a look-through sum of the parts. The group owns 59.5% of United Tractors directly and 62.1% effectively after its buybacks, 79.7% of Astra Agro Lestari and 76.9% of Astra Graphia, each at traded market capitalisation times that stake [S6]; UNTR is the whole mining division. Automotive and financial services are marked on nine-month 2026 attributable income annualised at four-thirds — IDR9.79tn and IDR7.15tn [S15] — not stale FY2025 earnings. The financing block uses its own book/ROE-COE card, not the parent's multiple: segment assets of IDR145.01tn less liabilities of IDR97.84tn earn an ROE on nine-month income above the 14.9% cost of equity, so it is carried at a justified premium to book [S15]. The toll roads, Serasi Autoraya and property stay on the group's own-history multiple because the four-segment disclosure no longer splits them [S0]. Holdco net cash of IDR1.80tn is added [S14]; property is marked on recurring earnings, stripping the IDR0.46tn bargain-purchase gain from the reported IDR0.72tn [S6, F29].

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: the P/E gives Rp5,911 and P/BV Rp6,647, respectively 26.9% and 42.7% away from the sum-of-the-parts [S0]. They diverge because the parts carry a 25% discount and the cross-checks none, and because P/BV uses the 30 September 2026 book value of IDR238.10tn [S15]. Rather than let that arithmetic narrow the discount, the cross-checks carry only 2% and 2% each; the target is the discounted sum-of-the-parts, with an effective discount within a point of the 25% held. The bases are Astra's own four-year average earnings multiple of 7.2x and book multiple of 1.1x from the pack's four annual observations, not a peer set [S0].

Today's price implies the variant view, and the implication has flipped in our favour. Solving for the holdco discount that reproduces Rp4,540, the market prices a 26.9% discount to our marks [S14, S2] — wider than the 25% we hold. That is the wide end of the name's own history: every one of the pack's four annual P/BV observations sits above today's 0.8x, and the shares have mostly traded at or above our NAV mark [S0]. The market is paying 5.6x FY2025 earnings against a four-year average of 7.2x and 0.8x book against 1.1x [S0]. Fixed-asset revaluation was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, so reported book needs no adjustment [S6]. For the price to be right, earnings must erode or the discount must widen further, both of which the bear case carries [S14].

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota, already cutting heavy-equipment demand and mining volumes, and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever [S14, S9]. Coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings, and mining is the most volatile block, so one weak quarter cannot be read as a recovery [S4, S14].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand; a consumer-durable and consumer-financing group is exposed on both the purchase decision and the credit book [S2, S4].

**Competitive and technology risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** Chinese entrants and the shift to electrified models threaten the auto franchise, which the group meets through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; automotive carries the top weight in the sum of the parts, so a share or mix loss is the largest value risk we carry [S9, S14].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block is IDR66.70tn of net debt against a receivables book of IDR132.00tn and grew new financing to IDR92.50tn; it is the most stable block and the most rate-sensitive. The bear case expresses it through a lower group margin, lower joint-venture and other income and a revenue-growth shock; the IDR1.16tn first-half provisioning charge is the credit-cost trend we watch [S5, S14, F35].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8]. The discount can widen while holders wait, which is why the base case holds it flat and the bull case carries the narrowing.

**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR232.7bn a day, and the parent received more in dividends than it paid in FY2025 while the interim was held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10]; a deeper mining downturn would pressure the payout.

The base case (50%) carries the actual nine months: revenue 1.0% this year and 5.0% thereafter, the higher cost ratio, the discount at 25%, and only the sourced buyback retirement (-1.3% this year, none next because no end date is disclosed); it gives Rp5,007. The bull case (25%) assumes share gains, a richer mix, the gold ramp and wider-business reallocation, the coal quota resetting and the buyback narrowing the discount below its persistent range; it values the shares at Rp5,969. The bear case (25%) assumes coal and palm oil weaken, the quota stays tight, credit costs rise, joint-venture income falls, auto share is lost and the discount widens to the top of its range; it values the shares at Rp4,043, below the current price. The shocks are mirrored — discount, revenue growth, gross margin and joint-venture contribution by the same magnitude — so an asymmetry needs a sourced reason and is not embedded [S14].

Signposts that would change our view: a wholesale run-rate consistent with the industry target while Astra's share holds [S7, S14]; Komatsu and mining-contractor volumes extending the third-quarter improvement [S14]; capital-allocation action on wider businesses [S11]; disclosed buyback execution [S8]; and any deterioration in upstream dividend coverage [S6].

Ownership is concentrated and stable. Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd held 50.1% at the last audited date and is part of the Jardine Matheson group; the free float is 49.0% [S6, S0]. No pledged controlling stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed, and minorities have no route to a control event; the route to value is the dividend, the buyback and the controller's decisions [S6, S8, S11].

Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025 and sales IDR27.94tn, principally the Honda, Toyota and Daihatsu joint ventures [S6]: operating architecture rather than value leakage, and both fell year on year [S6].

Capital actions are the main governance signal. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026, the IDR8.00tn Astra programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date, and the subsidiaries announced smaller programmes [S14, S16]. Astra is also offering for up to 4.95 per cent of Astra Otoparts at Rp3,600 a share, which would lift its stake to 84.95 per cent [S13, S14]; that moves value from minorities to the parent inside an already consolidated block, so our marks do not value it separately [S14]. The board has independent commissioners and a separately constituted audit committee, but the auditor's identity and opinion wording remain an open check because the archived LK omits the audit report text [S6].

Dividends per share were Rp650, Rp519, Rp406 and Rp390 across the last four financial years [S0], with a Rp98 interim declared for FY2026 at the prior year's level [S10]. On ESG, the material exposures are coal, palm oil and nickel, and the vehicle franchise's transition risk, which the group meets through its Japanese partners rather than a platform it owns [S14, S9].

The dated catalysts are the interim dividend paid at the end of October, the monthly wholesale data, the close of the Otoparts tender in November, and the FY2026 audited results in the spring, at which buyback execution must be disclosed [S10, S7, S14, S4]. The interim was held at the prior year's level despite the profit fall, a deliberate statement about payout durability [S10].

Between updates we monitor five things: national car wholesales and Astra's share [S7, S14]; Komatsu units and overburden for evidence the quota downturn has troughed [S14]; net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries [S14]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and the parent's dividends received against dividends paid, the most honest test of whether the distribution is funded by the operating businesses [S6].

bear.narrative: The national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the mining complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales down to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. Financial-services credit costs rise as a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro lifts arrears: the financing book carried a Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60]. The auto franchise loses share and mix to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9], JV income falls by Rp2,000bn, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, as the buyback fails to close it [S8, S14].

bull.narrative: The auto market reaches GAIKINDO's 850,000-unit target with Astra holding about half of it [S7, S4], the national coal quota resets and the mining complex stabilises (this is a bull assumption, not in the base), the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap add earnings - nine-month Others attributable profit was already Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S11, S14, F71] - share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin, and the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount to 10%, below the card's persistent range [S8, S14, S11].

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +1%: nine-month 2026 net revenue was Rp243.9tn, flat on the prior-year period [S14, S15], with the third quarter alone up about six per cent on the prior-year quarter as automotive and financial services grew; reaching +1% for the full year needs only a small fourth-quarter step-up, which the company guides to on mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued auto growth [S14]. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.69%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% [S15]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of revenue, the full-year rate implied by nine-month selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn [S15], with the third quarter at 10.84% as promotional spend normalised; the prior 10.14% FY2025 ratio no longer describes the run-rate. From FY2027E held at the third-quarter 10.84% [S15]: the three-quarter cost ratio is the last actual and no sourced cost programme justifies reverting to the pre-2026 10.14% ratio, so the forecast carries the higher run-rate rather than banking an unsourced efficiency gain.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, capex Rp17,440bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S0]; the group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 9.5%, the clean nine-month actual: reported profit for the period was Rp24,073bn including the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge, so clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn and clean profit attributable to non-controlling interests was about Rp2,471bn (Rp27,036bn less the Rp24,565bn clean parent profit), a 9.1% take [S12, S14, S15]. The mining business that carries United Tractors' 40.5% minority collapsed while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E set at 11.5% and 12% long run as a partial, not full, restoration toward the historical average: the Q3 mining recovery lifts the minority-heavy block but the mix remains toward wholly owned auto and financing [S14, S5]; a UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and other income.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual of 50% (cash dividends paid Rp16,426bn by the parent entity over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]); the company itself reports a 48% payout ratio for FY2025 on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4], and declared the same Rp98 interim for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at 0.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is described only as "still ongoing" in the 28 October 2026 release, and neither the EGM coverage nor the release fixes an end date or a 12-month window [S8, S14, S16]. With no dated execution period, further retirement is treated as upside in the bull case rather than built into the base; the completed to-September retirement is already in the FY2026E share count [S14].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 25%, inside the 20-40% persistent range the holdco method card makes the base rate. The name-specific test is whether that is wide against the shares' own history: across the data pack's four annual price observations the shares traded between roughly 0.9x and 1.2x book [S0], while today's price is 0.76x the 30 September 2026 book value of Rp5,999 a share [S15], so the current mark is at the wide end of the name's own range rather than the low end. The named, dated narrowing catalyst is the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM and still ongoing, alongside the May-2026 capital-allocation roadmap [S8, S14, S11]; with no disclosed buyback end date the base holds the discount flat and narrowing sits in the bull case.

challenges.challenge: At the held 25% discount the primary method is Rp4,250/share, 6.4% BELOW the Rp4,540 price, so the industry's primary method says the stock is not cheap. The Rp5,322 target is 25.2% above the primary method and requires the effective discount to fall from the market's 19.9% to about 6.1% (Rp5,323 against gross NAV of Rp5,666), because 40% of the blend - P/E 7.2x and P/BV 1.11x on own-history averages - is undiscounted. The base case says it holds the discount flat, but the blend closes roughly 20pp of it. The implied 19.9% is at or below the low end of the card's 20-40% persistent range, the opposite of the "enter when wide" rule, and no own-5y discount range is published although the output contract requires it. The rating is entirely dependent on this undefended narrowing.
challenges.answer: Re-marked the SOTP on the nine-month actuals (auto and financial services at the 9M run-rate, financing on book/ROE-COE, UNTR at the effective 62.12%, holdco net cash added) and re-based the target on the discounted SOTP. Weights are now 96/2/2, so the blend no longer closes the discount: the SOTP at the held 25% is Rp4,657, above the Rp4,540 price, and the price now implies a 26.9% discount, wider than we hold. The own-history range is published in section 4: every one of the pack's four annual P/BV observations sits above today's multiple, so the discount is at the wide end of the name's own history. Rating moves to ADD, target Rp5,006.

challenges.challenge: The only dated discount catalyst - and the basis for FY2027E share_change of -2.0% - is "the Rp8tn Astra programme ... runs to 16 July 2027 [S8]". The archived S8 (Beritasatu, 17 July 2026) reports the EGM approval of an Rp8tn buyback and mentions only a third period of 16 March-15 June 2026; it contains no 16 July 2027 date, no 12-month window and no end date. The frontmatter catalyst_date of 2027-07-16 is therefore uncited, and the second year of buyback retirement is unsourced.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced 16 July 2027 date from the frontmatter, section 7 and the share_change basis. Fetched S16 (Kompas, 17 July 2026), which confirms the EGM approval and states no end date or 12-month window. FY2027E share_change re-struck to 0.0% on the sourced period; the base carries only the completed to-September retirement. catalyst_date moved to 2027-04-30, the FY2026 audited-results date on the prior-year cadence [S4], when execution must be disclosed.

challenges.challenge: Financial Services - Rp64,467bn, 28.5% of the Rp226,203bn gross SOTP - is marked at the group's own 7.20x P/E on FY2025 net income of Rp8,952bn. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT requires an unlisted bank/multifinance part to be valued on its own house card (a bank sub via VAL_BANKS: book, ROE/COE, credit cost), never a blanket multiple. The same blanket 7.2x is also applied to automotive and infrastructure. The prior round raised this as FATAL (C2) and the response changed the multiple's source but not the method; a leveraged lender with Rp66.7tn of net debt against a Rp132tn receivables book cannot be valued on its parent's earnings multiple.
challenges.answer: Financial Services is no longer valued on the group P/E. Segment assets of Rp145,007bn less liabilities of Rp97,838bn give book equity of Rp47,169bn [S15, F73, F74]; nine-month attributable income of Rp7,152bn [S15, F69] earns a 20.2% ROE against the 14.94% COE, giving a justified P/B of 1.482x and a value of Rp69,921bn, carried as 9.776x the nine-month fact. The implied P/B, provisioning trend and credit cost are stated in sections 4 and 5.

challenges.challenge: Capital actions are carried only through share count. The Otoparts tender (4.95% at Rp3,600, about Rp858bn, lifting the stake from 80% to 84.95%) is explicitly "not valued separately"; the UNTR holding note records an effective 62.12% after UNTR's own buyback but the SOTP marks 59.50% (Rp51,960bn; at 62.12% it would be about Rp54,248bn, +Rp2.3tn); and the October UNTR Rp2tn and AALI Rp400bn buybacks, which lift the parent's look-through interest, get no value. The card says value everything the company owns.
challenges.answer: UNTR is now marked at the effective 62.12% post-buyback stake [S6, F72], adding about Rp2.3tn to the mark. The October UNTR and AALI buybacks are noted as value-neutral at market (a larger share of a smaller, cash-reduced company) and the Otoparts tender is explained as a transfer inside an already consolidated block with the maximum consideration disclosed. The remaining accretion is carried in the bull narrative. AUTO's standalone market price is not in our pack.

challenges.challenge: The wider businesses are improving but are marked on stale earnings with no upside path: 9M Others attributable profit was Rp2,558bn, +36% y/y, and agribusiness recovered on prices, yet Infrastructure (FY2025 Rp1,258bn) and Property (recurring Rp255bn) are capitalised on FY2025 at 7.2x. The May-2026 roadmap's reallocation into these businesses and the Martabe/gold ramp are named in section 1 but appear in no value; the bull only adds +3pp revenue, +1.2pp margin and Rp2,000bn of other income.
challenges.answer: The wider businesses' nine-month run-rate is disclosed (Others Rp2,558bn, +36% [S14, F71]) and the gold-ramp/reallocation path is carried in the bull narrative and the infra/property holding notes. We cannot mark infra and property on 9M earnings separately because the four-segment disclosure no longer splits them (S14/S15 show only the Others line); the last audited divisional split remains the sourced base, so the upside sits in the bull case rather than the base.

challenges.challenge: The bear target is Rp4,992, 9.9% ABOVE the Rp4,540 price, so even the bear case says buy, yet section 5 asserts that today's price needs only conditions "the bear case carries". The bear does not shock the financing book it names as the main risk (receivables Rp132tn, net debt Rp66.7tn, H1 provisioning Rp1,160bn) and does not shock Astra's auto share against Chinese and EV entrants, the largest unlisted block. Because the 10pp discount shock hits only the 60% SOTP leg while 40% of the blend stays undiscounted, the bear-base spread is only about 6% each way.
challenges.answer: The SOTP now carries 96% of the weight, so the discount shock hits almost the whole value. The bear widens the discount to 40% (the top of the card's 20-40% range, +0.15), cuts revenue growth, gross margin and JV/other income, and values the shares at Rp4,043, 10.9% below the price, producing absolute downside. The bear narrative names financing credit cost, auto share/mix and the discount, with sources.

challenges.challenge: The coal/RKAB risk is reduced to a 3pp revenue and 1.2pp margin haircut, with no volume, overburden, coal-price or JV-income path, although 9M Komatsu units fell 17%, overburden 7% and coal volumes 23%, and JV income (+20%) is the only line that rose. The bull assumes the quota "resets" with no source. MSHE was 21% of 9M clean profit and UNTR is 23% of gross SOTP, so this is the largest single earnings risk and it is the least modelled.
challenges.answer: The bear narrative now carries the sourced RKAB/coal path: Komatsu units 3,000 (-17%), overburden 766m bcm (-7%), coal 7.1Mt (-23%), gold 54k oz [S14, F53-F56], and compares H1-2026 MSHE profit with H1-2025 for the same period [S5, F30, F77]. The quota reset is stated as a bull-only assumption, not in the base.

challenges.challenge: Two of the three largest unlisted marks use FY2025 audited earnings although this update exists because Q3 is now known: automotive 9M Rp9,787bn is already 86% of FY2025's Rp11,365bn and financial services 9M Rp7,152bn is 80% of Rp8,952bn. At the held 7.2x that understates automotive by about Rp12.1tn and financial services by about Rp5.6tn, roughly Rp410/share gross (about Rp310 after the discount), and the report calls it "conservative" without a source. The most-likely standard bars unsourced conservatism exactly as it bars unsourced optimism.
challenges.answer: Automotive and financial services are marked on the nine-month attributable run-rate annualised (F68, F69) rather than FY2025; the report no longer calls the marks conservative. The resulting values are in sections 4 and the C1/C3 responses.

challenges.challenge: The SOTP bridge is zero. The card requires holdco net debt from the LK and holdco opex capitalised at about 10x; the September LK shows net cash of Rp1,800bn excluding the financing subsidiaries, and no holdco-opex charge appears anywhere. Separately, FY2026E minority of 14% sits above the actual clean 9M NCI share of 9.1% (reported total profit Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn charge = Rp27,036bn, NCI Rp2,471bn), and capex is held at 5.39% of revenue against a 3.29% H1 actual. The conservatism is not mirrored and is mostly unsourced.
challenges.answer: Added 9M holdco net cash of Rp1,800bn as a negative net-debt bridge [S14, F50]. On holdco opex, the parent-entity statement shows net revenue of Rp96,188bn and G&A of Rp4,519bn [S6, F78]: the parent is an operating distributor and that G&A is already inside the auto/distribution earnings, so charging it again would double count, and a separately identifiable holdco overhead is not disclosed. FY2026E minority reset to the 9.1% clean actual, then 11.5%/12% [S12, S14, S15]; capex kept at the FY2025 audited ratio as the last actual, with the lower H1 cash figure noted.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E SG&A is set at 10.135% of revenue, but the same basis records Q3 at 10.84% and the 9M actual is 11.22%. The text says it "reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate", which it does not: it is 70bp below Q3 and 108bp below the nine months, worth roughly Rp1.6-2.4tn of net profit - more than the whole FY2026E-FY2027E net profit increase of Rp826bn. The most likely path is the Q3 ratio, not the FY2025 one.
challenges.answer: FY2027E-2030E SG&A set at the Q3 10.84% [S15] instead of the FY2025 10.14%; the basis now says so and the model is re-run. The calibration gate is unchanged because it uses FY2026E, which was already at the nine-month rate.

challenges.challenge: other_nonop is set at Rp13,200bn for FY2026E and described as the "clean nine-month run-rate annualised". The clean run-rate is Rp8,661bn x 4/3 = Rp11,548bn (JV Rp8,127bn plus clean other income Rp534bn); even the basis's own figures give Rp10,836bn + Rp1,837bn = Rp12,673bn. The Rp13,200bn is 14% above the clean run-rate, unexplained, and it is the line that keeps FY2026E net profit flat while EBITDA falls 9%.
challenges.answer: other_nonop FY2026E rebuilt to Rp11,548bn = (JV Rp8,127bn + clean other income Rp534bn) x 4/3 [S15, S14, F66, F67], replacing Rp13,200bn; the arithmetic is shown in the basis.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E minority jumps from 14.0% to 21.37% in one year, a 7.4pp step worth about Rp3.2tn of net profit, with no bridge. The actual clean 9M minority is 9.1% and Q3 shows the mining block recovering while the mix shifts toward wholly owned auto and financing. The 3y-average restoration is not sourced and works against the base case's own mining-recovery thesis.
challenges.answer: Minority FY2026E set to the clean 9M actual 9.5% (NCI about Rp2,471bn on clean consolidated profit of about Rp27,036bn [S12, S14, S15]), then 11.5% in FY2027E and 12% long run as a partial restoration, not the three-year average 21.37%; the basis explains the UNTR-recovery link.

challenges.challenge: The multiple basis is described inconsistently: section 4 says "four-year average", the holdings notes and packet say "five-year average", and model own_history is n=4. The P/BV cross-check also uses 30 June equity (F37 Rp230,068bn) although 30 September equity (F49 Rp238,103bn) is in hand, worth about Rp40/share on the blend, and no PSAK-16 revaluation check is recorded before using book value, which EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS requires.
challenges.answer: Basis stated as four annual observations everywhere (model own_history n=4); P/BV switched to the 30 September 2026 equity of Rp238,103bn through a bs_equity fact [S15, F75]; the fixed-asset revaluation recorded as immaterial at Rp2bn [S6, F76].

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says H1-2026 MSHE net profit "fell to Rp607bn from Rp9,095bn in FY2025" - a half against a full year; the comparable H1-2025 figure is about Rp3,200bn. The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is also incomplete: no three-year accruals ratio is computed (only 9M OCF versus profit), and IDX board/notation status and the auditor are left as "open checks" although the card says the regime flags gate investability.
challenges.answer: Bear comparison fixed to H1-2025 Rp4,982bn [S5, F77] rather than FY2025; the three-year accruals position is stated from the pack (operating cash above net profit in FY2023-FY2025 [S0] and over nine months [S15]); the auditor and IDX notation are explicitly flagged as open checks because the archived LK omits the audit report and idx.co.id is not fetched by policy.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states that "every listed stake goes in at market value", but Astra Otoparts (AUTO.JK, 80% owned, 4.95% tendered at Rp3,600) sits inside the automotive block and 91.43% of PT Mega Manunggal Property Tbk (listed) sits inside the property block, both valued on a blanket multiple rather than at market. The card requires listed stakes at market value, and the report's own claim is therefore false.
challenges.answer: Corrected the 'every listed stake' sentence: only the stakes that are whole reported divisions (UNTR, AALI, ASGR) are marked at market; AUTO and the 91.43% MMPS are consolidated inside the automotive and property earnings blocks and are not marked a second time, avoiding double count. The reconciliation is stated in sections 4 and the holding notes.

missing_bull_case.note: Capital actions are read as share count only: the Otoparts tender (4.95% at Rp3,600, ~Rp858bn, 80% to 84.95%) is explicitly not valued, UNTR's effective 62.12% after its buyback is noted but the SOTP marks 59.50%, and the October UNTR Rp2tn / AALI Rp400bn buybacks get no value. Wider Businesses (9M Others Rp2,558bn, +36% y/y) are marked on FY2025 earnings with no upside path. C4, C5.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear target is Rp4,992, 9.9% above the Rp4,540 price, so every scenario is a buy; the financing book and auto share that section 5 names as the main risks are never shocked, and the discount shock hits only the 60% SOTP leg while 40% of the blend stays undiscounted. Coal/RKAB persistence is only a 3pp revenue and 1.2pp margin haircut, with no volume, overburden, coal-price or JV path. C6, C7.

assumption_realism.note: FY2027E SG&A at 10.135% sits below the Q3 10.84% the same basis cites and the 9M 11.22%; the text says it reproduces the Q3 exit, which it does not. other_nonop Rp13,200bn is 14% above the clean 9M annualised Rp11,548bn and cannot be reproduced from its own basis. FY2027E minority jumps 7.4pp to 21.37% with no bridge. C10, C11, C12.

evidence_and_citations.note: The dated catalyst "runs to 16 July 2027 [S8]" is not in S8, which only reports the 17 July 2026 EGM and a third buyback period of 16 March-15 June 2026; FY2027E share_change rests on it. The multiple basis is called four-year and five-year in different places; P/BV uses June equity when September equity is in hand; the bear narrative compares H1-2026 MSHE to FY2025. C2, C13, C14.

valuation_method_fit.note: The primary SOTP at the held 25% discount is Rp4,250, 6.4% below the price, and the target is 25% above the primary method: the blend embeds a 6% effective discount versus the 19.9% the market prices, so the base case closes about 20pp of discount through undiscounted P/E and P/BV rather than holding it flat. The card's 20-40% discount is the base rate and entry requires a wide, not narrow, discount; no own-5y range is published. Financial services, 28.5% of gross NAV, is on a blanket group P/E instead of the bank card; no holdco opex at 10x; AUTO and MMPS are listed but marked by multiple. C1, C3, C9, C15.

bias_and_tone.note: The thesis title "the parts are worth more than the group trades for" is false on the report's own numbers: the parts after the held discount are Rp4,250 against a Rp4,540 price. Section 5 says today's price needs only conditions "the bear case carries", yet the bear target is above that price. Prose asserts conservatism (FY2025 marks) while the target is driven by the most aggressive leg. C1, C6, C8.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Macro deck read correctly (usd_idr 18,350, BI 5.75%, CPI 3.28% for FY2027E) and the CAUTIOUS rate-sensitive posture is carried into the auto/financing discussion. Own-history multiples are the CONGLOMERATES industry mandate, and the 0.25 holdco discount matches the peer mode (ASII 0.25 in the peer set). Credit: the 9M anchor and the D&A restatement reconcile. C8 only.

conservatism_audit.note: Below-run-rate optics: auto and finserv marked on FY2025 though 9M is already 86% and 80% of it (~Rp410/share gross understated); 9M holdco net cash Rp1,800bn not added; holdco opex not capitalised at 10x; FY2026 minority 14% vs 9.1% actual; capex at 5.39% of revenue vs 3.29% H1; FY2027+ growth 5% vs ~8.6% nominal GDP. Against them: other_nonop Rp13,200bn, FY2027 SG&A 10.135%, and the blend discount. Neither side is sourced. C8, C9, C10, C11.

calibration.note: Engine QC returns no BLOCK flags. Calibration shows FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.10% vs FY2025A 17.48% (gap -1.39pp), which is explained by the sourced 9M SG&A ratio and Q4 at the Q3 rate, not an unsourced drift; the FY2026E minority, other_nonop and SG&A concerns are level issues the gate cannot see (C10-C12), not calibration failures.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. The three FATALs are answered on substance and the correction is coherent: C1 re-marks the unlisted blocks on 9M actuals and re-bases the target on the discounted SOTP (96/2/2); C2 removes the unsourced 16 Jul 2027 buyback date and re-strikes FY2027E share_change to 0; C3 values Financial Services on book/ROE-COE (1.48x P/B) instead of the parent P/E. The MATERIAL set C4-C12 and C15 is each answered on substance. Lint PASS, QC PASS with 0 BLOCK, judge PASS. The batch of one is not a systematic tilt against the published CONGLOMERATES peers (ADD 1, HOLD 3, SELL 4); ASII's 25% discount sits inside the card range, and it is narrower than the peers' 30% only because the price already implies 26.9% and the shares sit at 0.8x book against a 0.9-1.2x own-history range. The open Q1 FIX is real but immaterial to the published numbers: the Rp1,800bn 'holdco net cash' equals the three non-financing divisions' own net positions already inside their equity marks, so removing it costs about Rp45/share gross; target about Rp4,970 and TR about 18.7%, still ADD, with the SOTP still above the price. Q3 (about 1.3% of NAV) is likewise sub-material. Both should be corrected at the next version. Non-value-bearing nit for the next version: catalyst_date 2027-04-30 cites S4, which is the 26 Feb 2026 FY2025 release and does not fix that date (prior-year cadence implies late Feb 2027). No contamination met; no positions or P&L.

bias.note: The earnings forecast is if anything below last actual: FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.10% vs FY2025A 17.48% (-1.39pp), sourced to the 9M actual SG&A of 11.22% and Q3 10.84% [S15]; FY2027E+ revenue growth of 5% and terminal growth of 4% sit below the macro deck implied nominal 8.57%. Against that, automotive and financial services are marked on 9M annualised run-rates (Rp13,049bn and Rp9,536bn, +15% and +6.5% on FY2025 [S14, S15]), the 25% discount held is 1.9pp narrower than the 26.9% the price implies [S0], and payout is 50% vs the company stated 48% [S4]. Every driver cites a source; net direction neutral.

recomputed.item: 9M2026 Financial Services book equity (assets 145,007 less liabilities 97,838)
9M2026 Financial Services attributable segment income (mark input)

findings.finding: valuation.holdco_net_debt adds Rp1,800bn described as holdco net cash, but S14 defines it as net cash excluding the Group Financial Services subsidiaries; the segment note shows the three non-financing blocks sum to the same -1,787 (auto net cash 2,499, MSHE net debt 4,478, wider net cash 3,766 [S15]), and all three are already marked at equity values (UNTR at market, auto and wider on P/E), so the centre line double counts their net positions. Worth about Rp45 per share.

The -1.39pp FY2026E vs FY2025A EBITDA-margin gap is real and sourced, not drift: the FY2025 P&L reconciles exactly (gross profit 71,444 less selling 11,744 and G&A 21,035 gives EBIT 38,665, plus D&A 17,871 gives EBITDA 56,536 [S6]), and the lower forward margin comes from 9M SG&A of 11.22% and Q3 of 10.84% [S15]. Note the P&L forecast does not feed the primary SOTP, which is struck on segment marks.

The Financial Services ROE base of Rp47,169bn excludes the Rp9,284bn of investments in joint ventures and associates shown in the same segment note [S15]. If any part of the Rp7,152bn attributable income is equity-accounted, the 20.2% ROE and the 1.482x justified P/B are overstated; including those investments in the book would cut the block by roughly Rp3tn (about 1.3% of NAV).

Payout is held at 50%, but the company reports 48% for FY2025 (Rp390 on EPS Rp810 [S4]); the Rp16,426bn cash-dividend figure in F22 spans the prior-year final and is not an FY2025 payout. DPS of Rp420 would be about Rp403 at 48%. The total return is unaffected because the target is struck net of DPS, but the DPS line is high.

The post_bs_review note opens by saying it searched since the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, although the balance-sheet date is now 30 September 2026. The content does cover post-September events (2 October interim, 13 October to 11 November Otoparts tender, October to December UNTR and AALI buybacks).

The weights.changed justification cites [S0, S15], which support the inputs but not the 96/2/2 weight choice; the authority is VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT, not those sources. The flag is WARN and the choice is the red-team fix, so it is not blocking.

FY2027E+ revenue growth of 5% is 3.6pp below the macro deck implied nominal 8.57% (5.29% real plus 3.28% inflation); the basis gives a rationale but no source. It is immaterial to the target because revenue feeds only the unused DCF and the 2% P/E cross-check, not the SOTP marks.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The SOTP is the CONGLOMERATES primary per VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT; P/E and P/BV carry only a nominal 2% each so undiscounted cross-checks cannot close the holdco discount, which the red team showed the old 60/25/15 blend did [S0, S15].
